title: Scrub environment-specific references from plan.md and refresh stale sections; keep station benchmark generic
description:
docs/plan/plan.md is in a public repo but still references the maintainer's private build/deployment environments and hints at a specific downstream consumer. A prior pass (commit 49c04c8) genericized most of it; residuals remain:

1. Line ~26 (design principle 5): names a specific internal CI cluster. Rephrase to "local or CI" without the internal name.
2. Lines ~189-190 (Phase 0) and ~263 (Open Questions): "on an internal cluster... not the VPS" — private deployment topology. Rephrase to "on a host with the reference toolchain installed".
3. Line ~223 (Phase 7): "consumed by a downstream backtest join" — hints at the consuming application domain. Rephrase to a neutral consumer, e.g. "consumed by downstream time-series analysis".

The fixed-station benchmark section (20 US metro METAR stations) must STAY exactly as-is — it is deliberately generic; do not tie it to any application or narrow its framing.

Also refresh stale content while in the file (this is the single plan-update pass):
4. "Crate layout (workspace)" section omits crates/gribtract-testutil and crates/gribtract-py, and lists a repo-root tests/ directory — integration tests actually live at crates/gribtract/tests/ (differential.rs, station_extraction.rs). Align with the real workspace.
5. docs/notes/station-extraction-benchmark.md "Definition of done" checkboxes are all unticked although the harness, both modes, the dashboard view, and docs/notes/parse-speed-log.md all exist — tick what is true (leave the bilinear-verification box to bf-6bxh).

Acceptance criteria:
- grep of docs/ finds no internal cluster/CI/host names and no deployment-environment references.
- No wording that identifies or hints at a specific downstream application.
- Crate layout section matches Cargo.toml workspace members.
- Note checkboxes reflect implemented reality.

title: Implement Rotated Lat/Lon grid definition template -- plan Phase 5 names it, code does not have it
description:
plan.md Phase 5 (marked complete) reads: "Grid geometry breadth. Lambert conformal (HRRR native), polar stereographic, Gaussian, rotated. Geometry must match for point asof-joins." Three of those four projections are implemented; rotated is not.

Evidence:
- crates/gribtract-core/src/decode.rs, the parse_section3 template dispatch, only matches grid definition template numbers 0 (lat/lon), 20 (polar stereographic), 30 (Lambert conformal), 40 (Gaussian lat/lon); every other template number, including 1 (rotated lat/lon), falls through to the NotImplemented error.
- crates/gribtract-core/src/types.rs GridProjection enum has exactly 4 variants: LatLon, PolarStereographic, LambertConformal, GaussianLatLon -- no Rotated or RotatedLatLon variant exists anywhere in the codebase.
- Searched all 49 open beads for the word "rotated" (case-insensitive) -- zero matches. This gap is not already tracked by any existing or deferred bead.

Any real GRIB2 file using a rotated-pole grid (common in some regional and limited-area ensemble products) will currently fail to decode at all.

Scope (keep this narrow -- do not chase a NOAA archive fetch; follow the existing bootstrap pattern already used for the DRT 2, 40, 41 and PDT 1, 8 templates, which shipped as small python-generated synthetic fixtures under scripts, e.g. gen_grib2_drt2.py, before any real fixtures were sourced separately):
1. Add a RotatedLatLon projection variant to GridProjection in types.rs (fields per the WMO grid definition template for rotated lat/lon: south pole latitude, south pole longitude, angle of rotation, plus the same Ni, Nj, lat_first, lon_first, lat_last, lon_last, di, dj fields already used for the plain lat/lon template).
2. Add a parse function for this template to decode.rs and wire template number 1 into the parse_section3 match arm.
3. Implement the nearest-point-index lookup for the rotated case (rotate the query point into the rotated-pole frame, then reuse the existing plain lat/lon arithmetic).
4. Add a synthetic fixture via a new generator script (following the pattern of scripts/gen_grib2_drt2.py) and its golden JSON, wired into tests/corpus/manifest.json and the differential suite.

Acceptance criteria:
- The rotated lat/lon grid template decodes successfully (no more NotImplemented error) for the new fixture.
- The new synthetic rotated-grid fixture appears in tests/corpus/manifest.json and passes the differential suite (cargo test -p gribtract --test differential).
- A nearest-point-index unit test exists for the new RotatedLatLon projection, covering at least the grid corners and center.

title: ProviderProbe::default_probe_files() uses hardcoded stale date (20250702) — runtime live re-probe fallback is broken
description:
plan.md's "Provider probe & selection" component, step 5, specifies: "At runtime, the fetch layer loads provider-probe.json on startup and falls back to re-probing live if the file is absent, stale (>24h), or if a provider returns HTTP errors on N consecutive requests." The runtime entry point for this is `ProviderProbe::new()` in `crates/gribtract-fetch/src/probe.rs` -- the exact API documented in `crates/gribtract-fetch/README.md`'s own usage example.

Verified: `ProviderProbe::new()` and `with_client()` both populate `probe_files` from `Self::default_probe_files()` (probe.rs ~line 74), which hardcodes 8 probe URLs (HRRR, GEFS, NBM, GFS x S3/GCS/NOMADS) all containing the literal date string "20250702", e.g. `https://noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/hrrr.20250702/conus/hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf00.grib2.idx`. NOAA's public buckets only retain files for a rolling window (days to a few months depending on model); this hardcoded date is now well outside that window, so every one of these URLs will 404 on any live re-probe attempt -- silently breaking exactly the "falls back to re-probing live" reliability path the plan requires.

This is a distinct bug from bf-3901 (already tracked -- the missing consecutive-HTTP-error *trigger* for re-probing). This bug is in the probe *execution* itself, once a re-probe is triggered by any means (staleness, absence, or bf-3901's future trigger).

Contrast: the separate `xtask probe-providers` command (`xtask/src/probe_providers.rs`) does this correctly -- it has a `days_ago`-based helper that computes a real `YYYYMMDD` from `chrono::Utc::now()` at call time and substitutes it into `{date}`/`{hour}` placeholder URLs, rather than hardcoding a literal date.

What to do:
1. In `crates/gribtract-fetch/src/probe.rs`, replace the hardcoded "20250702" literals in `default_probe_files()` with a dynamically computed recent date. Mirror the logic already used by `xtask/src/probe_providers.rs`'s `days_ago`-style date helper (e.g. a few days lookback to allow for publish lag) rather than reinventing it -- consider whether this date-computation logic should be extracted to a shared helper both crates call, to avoid two independent implementations drifting apart again.
2. Add a unit test asserting the generated probe URLs in `default_probe_files()` contain a recently-computed date (e.g. within the last N days of `chrono::Utc::now()`), not a fixed literal string.
3. Confirm the existing `test_probe_hrrr" test (probe.rs ~line 322) still passes.

Acceptance criteria:
- No hardcoded YYYYMMDD literal remains in `default_probe_files()`.
- `cargo test -p gribtract-fetch` passes.
- A new or updated test confirms the probe URL date tracks the current date rather than a fixed string.

title: No CI wired for gribtract: dashboard-artifact publishing (plan Phase 2b) has no Argo WorkflowTemplate in declarative-config
description:
docs/notes/throughput-dashboard.md "Definition of done" lists: "CI publishes the dashboard as an artifact on each build", and the "Reproducibility contract" section says "CI runs the benchmark on a pinned runner and publishes the dashboard as a build artifact ... each tagged by host, so they're never conflated." plan.md Phase 2b names the dashboard as wired in early (Phase 2) and updated forever after.

Verified: listing the Argo Workflows CI-template directory for the iad-ci cluster inside jedarden/declarative-config (the k8s config tree, under iad-ci, argo-workflows) and grepping case-insensitively for "grib" returns nothing -- there is no WorkflowTemplate for gribtract at all. This is unlike comparable pure-Rust-tool repos that already have a dedicated CI template in that same directory (forge-ci for jedarden/forge, needle-ci for jedarden/NEEDLE, agentscribe-ci for jedarden/AgentScribe, sigil-ci for jedarden/SIGIL). Currently gribtract only gets the generic, repo-agnostic `cargo test` auto-offload (the `rust-verify` template: fmt+clippy+test) triggered transparently by the local cargo wrapper -- there is no CI step anywhere that runs `cargo run --bin xtask -- bench` and publishes `dashboard.html` / `bench-results.json` as a build artifact.

What to do:
1. In jedarden/declarative-config, add a new WorkflowTemplate (e.g. `gribtract-ci`) alongside the other per-repo CI templates in that same Argo Workflows directory (iad-ci cluster config tree). Copy the structure of an existing same-class template (sigil-ci or agentscribe-ci are the closest match -- Rust binary/library repo, no container build) rather than inventing a new shape.
2. The template should, on trigger: checkout jedarden/gribtract, run `cargo test` (differential suite must stay green -- this is the correctness gate per plan.md's oracle-first design law, do not skip it), then run `cargo run --bin xtask -- bench` to regenerate `bench-results.json`/`dashboard.html`, and publish both as Argo Workflow `outputs.artifacts`.
3. No new secrets should be required beyond whatever the existing sibling templates already use for git checkout.
4. Commit and push the new template file to jedarden/declarative-config's `origin` remote (that repo pushes to `origin`/GitHub directly, not Forgejo -- follow that repo's own conventions). The ArgoCD app that syncs the iad-ci Argo Workflows templates will pick it up automatically -- do not `kubectl apply` it directly.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new WorkflowTemplate file exists in jedarden/declarative-config's Argo Workflows CI-template directory, committed and pushed.
- A manually submitted workflow run against the new template (per the "Submitting a workflow manually" pattern) completes successfully and produces a `dashboard.html` + `bench-results.json` artifact.

title: Fix differential coverage report: agreement_pct() can exceed 100% (double-subtracts jpeg2000-skipped fixtures)
description:
Verified by running: cargo test -p gribtract --test differential -- --nocapture (default features, jpeg2000 OFF, which is the default cargo test path used by the sub-minute verify loop).

Actual output:
=== Differential Harness Coverage ===
Fixtures : 7 total  (4 comparable, 3 no-golden)
  matched      : 6
  decode errors: 0
Agreement: 6/4 (150.0%)

matched (6) exceeds comparable (4) -- a mathematically impossible ratio that still passes AGREEMENT_FLOOR = 100.0 in crates/gribtract/tests/differential.rs.

Root cause (crates/gribtract/tests/differential.rs + crates/gribtract-testutil/src/diff.rs):
- The 2 DRT=40 (JPEG2000) fixtures are skipped BEFORE report.fixtures_total is incremented (the #[cfg(not(feature = "jpeg2000"))] branch does report.fixtures_no_golden += 1; continue; without touching fixtures_total).
- CoverageReport::agreement_pct() in diff.rs computes comparable = fixtures_total.saturating_sub(fixtures_no_golden). Since the 2 jpeg2000-skipped fixtures were never added to fixtures_total but ARE counted in fixtures_no_golden, they get subtracted a second time, undercounting comparable (4 instead of the true 6) while fixtures_matched (6) is correct.
- With --features jpeg2000 enabled the bug is masked (fixtures_total=9, no_golden=2, matched=7, comparable=7, agreement=100.0% -- correct), which is presumably why this has gone unnoticed: the default (no-feature) cargo test path used by the marathon loop is the one thats broken.

This corrupts the (a) agreement-coverage gate that plan.md names as the first-priority, top-level pass/fail signal for the whole differential harness (design principle 1: "the oracle is the product"). A future AGREEMENT_FLOOR increase or regression could be silently masked by this overcounting.

Also fix the stale top-of-file doc comment in differential.rs ("Passes at 0% agreement -- the framework is wired but the decoder is not yet implemented") which is no longer true (6+ templates now decode and match).

Acceptance criteria:
- Either track no_golden separately from the jpeg2000-feature-skip counter, or increment fixtures_total for all inline fixtures unconditionally (matching what happens when the feature is enabled) so comparable = fixtures_total - fixtures_no_golden is always accurate.
- Add a unit test in gribtract-testutil/src/diff.rs asserting agreement_pct() never exceeds 100.0 for a synthetic CoverageReport with skipped + no-golden + matched fixtures mixed.
- cargo test -p gribtract --test differential -- --nocapture (default features) prints a comparable count that equals the actual number of fixtures that were golden-loaded and compared (currently should read 6, not 4).
- Update/remove the stale 0%-agreement doc comment at the top of differential.rs.

title: gribtract-core claims no_std-friendly (Cargo.toml + plan.md) but unconditionally depends on std
description:
`crates/gribtract-core/Cargo.toml`'s `description` field reads: "Low-level GRIB2 section parser and template decoders — no_std-friendly". plan.md's architecture diagram labels the same crate "gribtract-core (no_std-friendly where able)". This description is public-facing metadata that will ship to crates.io if/when the crate is published (see the separate, related crates.io-publish-status gap filed in this same audit).

Verified the claim is false for every current build configuration:
- `grep -rn no_std crates/gribtract-core/src crates/gribtract-core/Cargo.toml` finds only the description string itself -- no `#![no_std]` attribute, no `no_std` feature gate, anywhere in the crate.
- `crates/gribtract-core/src/error.rs` unconditionally does `use std::fmt;` and `impl std::error::Error for Error`, with no `#[cfg]` guard.
- The crate's `Cargo.toml` `[features]` table has only `default = []` and `jpeg2000 = ["jpeg2k"]` -- no `std`/`no_std`-related feature exists to opt out of.

What to do -- pick ONE of these two fixes (do not attempt a full no_std port unless choosing B):
A) (preferred for an unattended worker -- low risk) Remove the "no_std-friendly" wording from `crates/gribtract-core/Cargo.toml`'s `description` field and from plan.md's architecture diagram, replacing it with an accurate description, e.g. "Low-level GRIB2 section parser and template decoders".
B) (larger, only if there is a concrete reason to actually want no_std support) Gate std usage behind a `std` feature (default-on), add `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]` to lib.rs, and convert `std::fmt`/`std::error::Error` usage in error.rs to `core`-only equivalents. Verify `cargo build -p gribtract-core --no-default-features` compiles standalone.

Given no downstream consumer in this workspace currently needs true no_std (gribtract-fetch, gribtract-cli, and gribtract-py all pull in std freely), option A is the appropriate fix.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either: `grep -rn no_std crates/gribtract-core/Cargo.toml docs/plan/plan.md` finds no unqualified "no_std-friendly" claim (option A), or: `cargo build -p gribtract-core --no-default-features` genuinely succeeds under a real no_std configuration (option B).

title: Expand differential corpus with real remote-stored fixtures: Lambert DRT=3, real ensemble, Gaussian, CONUS DRT=0, full multi-hour cycle
description:
Plan design principle 2 says "Real files only. Fixtures are actual NOAA grib2 messages... not synthetic", but 6 of the 9 fixtures in tests/corpus/manifest.json are synthetic 3x3/3x2 grids generated by scripts/gen_grib2*.py. All 9 are storage=inline; no remote fixture exists even though `xtask corpus fetch` (remote storage + sha256 verification, bf-1xsf) is implemented and unused.

Missing real-data coverage, in priority order:
1. A real Lambert-conformal (GDT 3.30) + complex-packing (DRT=3) file — the native combination for high-resolution regional models; currently GDT 3.30 is verified only against a synthetic fixture.
2. A real ensemble/statistical product (PDT 4.1 / 4.8) — currently synthetic only.
3. A real Gaussian-grid (GDT 3.40) file — currently synthetic only.
4. A CONUS-covering DRT=0 (simple packing) field — docs/notes/parse-speed-log.md (Baseline and Attempt 1) records that the lazy DRT=0 point-extraction speedup is unmeasurable because the only DRT=0 fixture covers 0-40N/0-40E with no US stations in range.
5. A full model cycle for one field (40+ forecast-hour messages) — Attempt 3 in the same log names this as the prerequisite for retrying parallel extraction and for a meaningful stations-x-hours benchmark.

What to do: source the files from public NOAA archives, record provenance in the manifest, store large files remotely (storage=remote, sha256) fetched via `cargo xtask corpus fetch`, generate goldens with the reference decoder (scripts/gen_golden.py pattern), and wire them into the differential suite and the station benchmark.

Acceptance criteria:
- tests/corpus/manifest.json gains at least 4 real fixtures covering items 1-4 (item 5 may be a follow-up).
- At least the large ones use storage=remote and fetch+verify cleanly.
- Differential suite passes with the new fixtures at 100% agreement (or disagreements become ratcheted fixtures with beads).
- Station benchmark reports in_range > 0 for the CONUS DRT=0 fixture and the lazy-path speedup number becomes meaningful.

description:
## Genesis Bead

## Overview

- [ ] Phase 1: Framing + metadata
- [ ] Phase 2: Simple packing (5.0) + lat/lon grid (3.0)

- [ ] Phase 4: JPEG2000 (5.40) + PNG (5.41)
- [ ] Phase 5: Grid geometry breadth
- [ ] Phase 6: Ensembles + statistical products (GEFS)
- [ ] Phase 7: Publish + integrate

title: Add station-extraction correctness test for CONUS data (DRT=3)
description:
Problem: the differential harness verifies full-grid decode against eccodes golden for gfs_tmp2m_1deg_anl (DRT=3, 360x181), but there is no #[test] that verifies station point-extraction against known-good values for this real CONUS-covering fixture. The bench harness does a verification pass comparing extracted values against full-grid decode, but that is a throughput run with agreement logged as a float, not a persistent correctness assertion.

What to do: add a new #[test] (in crates/gribtract/tests/differential.rs or a new crates/gribtract/tests/station_extraction.rs) that:
1. Loads gfs_tmp2m_1deg_anl.grib2 (inline, DRT=3, global 1-deg, GFS 2m temperature).
2. Calls gribtract::decode() to get the fully-decoded Field.
3. For each of the 7 CONUS stations in bench_station::STATIONS, calls field.grid.nearest_index(lat, lon) and field.values.get_at(idx).
4. Derives expected values from the existing full-grid golden JSON (tests/corpus/golden/gfs_tmp2m_1deg_anl.json) by looking up the same grid index. Tolerance = one LSB of the packing.
5. Asserts all 7 stations return Some(value) -- they must be in range of a 360x181 global grid.
6. Asserts extracted value == golden value within tolerance.

Acceptance criteria:
- cargo test station_extraction passes.
- All 7 stations covered: New York (40.78N/-73.97), Philadelphia (39.87N/-75.23), Chicago (41.79N/-87.75), Miami (25.79N/-80.29), Austin (30.32N/-97.76), Denver (39.85N/-104.66), Los Angeles (33.94N/-118.41).
- Tolerance is derived from packing parameters, not a magic epsilon.
- No new fixture file needed.

Notes: This test becomes the persistent gate for 'station extraction works on real GFS DRT=3 data.' All 7 stations are within the 360x181 global grid so nearest_index must return Some(_) for all.

title: ProviderProbe: implement the consecutive-HTTP-error re-probe trigger specified in plan.md (only the 24h staleness trigger exists)
description:
plan.md, the "Provider probe and selection" component (Phase 7, marked complete), step 5 states verbatim: "At runtime, the fetch layer loads provider-probe.json on startup and falls back to re-probing live if the file is absent, stale (>24h), or if a provider returns HTTP errors on N consecutive requests."

Three trigger conditions are specified: file absent, file stale (over 24 hours), and N consecutive HTTP errors from a provider. Checked the implementation in crates/gribtract-fetch/src/probe.rs:
- load_results handles the absent-file case -- it returns a Result, so absence is a normal error path callers can react to.
- is_stale(results, max_age) explicitly handles the 24-hour staleness case, with a doc comment saying exactly that.
- The third condition is entirely absent. A repo-wide search for consecutive, circuit, reprobe, re-probe, error_count and failure_count across crates/gribtract-fetch/src and crates/gribtract/src returns zero matches in either crate.

There is no per-provider failure counter, no threshold N, and no code path that triggers a re-probe based on live request failures -- only the 24-hour TTL check exists. This is a plan-specified reliability behavior (the whole point of probing multiple providers is to route around one that started failing mid-deployment) with no implementation at all, not a partial or buggy one.

Scope (keep this narrow, no network fixture needed -- this can be built and tested with a counter and a mock or fake failing endpoint):
1. Add a per-provider consecutive-failure counter to FetchClient, or a thin wrapper around it, in crates/gribtract-fetch (client.rs or probe.rs).
2. Define a threshold N for consecutive failures before re-probing (plan.md does not pin a specific number -- pick a reasonable default, e.g. 3, and make it configurable).
3. Expose a method, e.g. should_reprobe(provider) returning a bool, that callers can check alongside the existing is_stale check.
4. Reset the counter to zero on a successful request for that provider.
5. Add a unit test that simulates N consecutive failures for one provider and asserts should_reprobe returns true for it, asserts a subsequent success resets it back to false, and asserts a different provider's counter is unaffected by the first provider's failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- New consecutive-failure tracking exists in gribtract-fetch with a unit test covering the trigger and the reset.
- The runtime provider-selection logic, wherever provider-probe.json is loaded and consulted, checks should_reprobe alongside the existing staleness check, not staleness alone.
- cargo test -p gribtract-fetch passes with the new tests.

title: Parse-speed track: per-width specialized group extractors for DRT=3 (next Phase 2c iteration)
description:
Plan Phase 2c is an open-ended optimization track that is never done; when no correctness bead is the obvious pick, advancing it is always valid work. This bead is the next concrete iteration, seeded from the techniques log.

docs/notes/parse-speed-log.md Attempt 2 ("Implication for DRT=3 speed") names the follow-up: specialize per-group extraction for the most common group widths in complex packing (typically w=0, 4, 8, 12) — a dispatch keyed on width returning a branch-free extractor, removing the residual per-element branching that Attempt 4 (windowed u64 extractor, +17.6%) did not eliminate. A further option is std::arch SIMD intrinsics behind #[target_feature(enable="avx2")] with a scalar fallback.

Rules of the track (from plan.md):
- Correctness gates speed: 100% differential agreement must hold; a faster path that changes any value is a regression.
- Measure stations-x-hours/sec and MB/s before/after with `cargo xtask bench` on the same fixtures; keep the change only if it wins.
- Either way, append an entry to docs/notes/parse-speed-log.md (technique, result, why) — a documented dead end is a valid outcome; revert the code if it does not help.

Touch points: crates/gribtract-core/src/decode.rs (decode_drt3, extract_group_windowed), xtask/src/bench.rs, xtask/src/bench_station.rs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A new Attempt entry exists in docs/notes/parse-speed-log.md with before/after numbers.
- Differential suite passes at 100% agreement.
- Code kept only on a measured win; otherwise reverted with the log entry explaining why.

title: README claims are ahead of the implementation: pure-Rust/no-FFI claim, CLI section, cargo bench command
description:
README.md makes three claims that are currently false, in a public repo:

1. "No C dependencies... No FFI wrappers" / "Pure Rust — no C toolchain, no FFI": crates/gribtract-core/Cargo.toml line 14 depends on jpeg2k with the openjpeg-sys feature — C FFI to OpenJPEG — used for DRT 5.40 (JPEG2000) decode. plan.md Open Questions explicitly left this unresolved.
2. The CLI section documents `gribtract decode|list|dump` with examples, but crates/gribtract-cli/src/main.rs is a 4-line stub that prints "not yet implemented" and exits 1 (tracked separately as bf-2r2q).
3. "Run benchmarks and regenerate bench-results.json: cargo bench" — there are no cargo bench targets in the workspace; the actual command is `cargo xtask bench`.

What to do:
- For (1), preferred fix: make JPEG2000 support an optional cargo feature (e.g. `jpeg2000`, off by default or clearly documented), so the default build is genuinely pure Rust; alternatively evaluate a pure-Rust J2K decoder that passes the existing DRT=40 fixtures (tests/corpus/small/drt40_j2k_3x2.grib2, gfswave_arctic_wind_drt40.grib2) within derived tolerance. If neither is feasible now, amend the README to state the scoped C dependency honestly (5.40 only).
- For (2), either implement via bf-2r2q first or mark the CLI section as pending.
- For (3), correct the command to `cargo xtask bench`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every claim in README.md is true of a fresh default `cargo build`.
- If a feature flag is introduced, the differential suite still passes with the feature enabled, and DRT=40 fixtures are skipped (not silently passed) when disabled.
- README benchmark instructions reproduce bench-results.json.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Research completed. Documented NOAA ensemble product types (GEFS, SREF, NAEFS), their PDT usage (4.1 for individual members, 4.8 for statistical processing), and naming conventions. Key findings:

- PDT 4.1: Individual ensemble forecasts (control + perturbed members)

title: P2c speed: DRT=3 lazy/partial-decode fast path for station extraction
description:
Problem: the lazy bench path (run_lazy_nearest in xtask/src/bench_station.rs) only handles DRT=0 fields. For DRT=3 (complex packing with spatial differencing -- the GFS 1-degree product, gfs_tmp2m_1deg_anl), section7_raw is left empty in decode_bytes_lazy (see decode.rs line 1021: 'let drt0 = builder.drt_template == Some(0)'), so run_lazy_nearest skips all DRT=3 fields and reports in_range=0. The bench is vacuously fast because no real work is done for CONUS stations on the real GFS fixture.

What to do: (1) In decode.rs, extend decode_lazy_message to also store section7_raw for DRT=3 fields. (2) Add decode_point_drt3(body, packing, extra, idx) that full-decodes section 7 using the DRT=3 path and returns values[idx] -- not true random access (spatial differencing prevents that) but avoids re-parsing sections 0-6 per call. (3) Expose the new function from gribtract/src/lib.rs. (4) Extend run_lazy_nearest in bench_station.rs to also bench DRT=3 lazy fields. (5) Extend the verify pass in bench_station.rs for DRT=3 lazy path agreement.

Acceptance criteria: xtask bench --workload station-extract shows in_range > 0 for a DRT=3 lazy path row (should be 7 from gfs_tmp2m_1deg_anl). Agreement for DRT=3 lazy path is 1.0. cargo test passes.

Note: for DRT=3, true random access is not possible without full grid decode because spatial differencing means each value depends on all prior values. Document this constraint in the techniques log (docs/notes/station-extraction-benchmark.md). The real optimization win for DRT=3 is caching the decoded grid across multiple station lookups on the same field -- that is a separate bead.

title: OPS-GATED: crates.io publish claimed complete (bf-1pyo closed) but gribtract/gribtract-core are not live on crates.io
description:
plan.md Phase 7 ("Publish + integrate", marked [x] complete) names crates.io as a deliverable. Bead bf-1pyo ("Publish workspace crates 0.1.0 to crates.io") is closed, and its sibling bf-332u ("P7.1: crates.io publish prep - metadata, dry-run, README") suggests only the dry-run/prep step happened.

Verified directly against the crates.io API (User-Agent header required or crates.io rejects the request; confirmed the call format works via a control check against a known-real crate):

  curl -H 'User-Agent: audit' https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/gribtract
  -> {"errors":[{"detail":"crate `gribtract` does not exist"}]}

  curl -H 'User-Agent: audit' https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/gribtract-core
  -> {"errors":[{"detail":"crate `gribtract-core` does not exist"}]}

Neither crate is actually live. The declarative-config repo's CI-templates area (under k8s, for the iad-ci cluster's Argo Workflows) has a disabled ExternalSecret manifest that provisions a crates.io publish token for the pdftract project specifically -- named along the lines of "crates io token pdftract externalsecret, disabled" -- which is the established pattern for provisioning a crates.io publish token in this workspace. No equivalent exists for gribtract, consistent with the real `cargo publish` step never having run.

docs/notes/publish-guide.md documents the exact manual sequence: `cargo login`, then `cargo publish -p gribtract-core`, wait ~60s for indexing, `cargo publish -p gribtract`, wait, `cargo publish -p gribtract-cli`.

This requires a crates.io API token (a secret not available to an unattended worker) and is an irreversible public action -- crates.io does not allow un-publishing a version. OPS-GATED: do not attempt to obtain, fabricate, or guess a crates.io token, and do not run `cargo publish`.

What a human should do: either (a) provision a crates.io token following the disabled pdftract pattern referenced above and run the publish sequence in docs/notes/publish-guide.md, or (b) decide the crates should stay unpublished for now and correct plan.md's Phase 7 checkbox plus bf-1pyo's close reason to reflect that accurately, so the tracking record isn't false.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either gribtract and gribtract-core are confirmed live on crates.io (curl https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/gribtract returns crate data, not a does-not-exist error), or plan.md and bf-1pyo are corrected to no longer claim this is done, with the real status documented.

title: DRT 5.4 (IEEE 32-bit float) data representation template is named in plan.md but never implemented
description:
plan.md's "Template Registry" component lists Data Representation Templates (5.x) as: "how values are packed: simple, complex, complex+spatial-differencing, IEEE float, JPEG2000, PNG." "IEEE float" is GRIB2 Data Representation Template 5.4. docs/notes/oracle-and-tolerance.md further specifies its comparison rule explicitly: "IEEE-float templates (5.4) are compared exactly (bit-identical)."

Verified in code: `crates/gribtract-core/src/decode.rs`, function `parse_section5` (~line 908), matches template numbers 0, 2, 3, 40, 41 only; template 4 falls through to `_ => Err(Error::NotImplemented)` at line 936. Evidence -- the manifest at tests/corpus/manifest.json has provenance blocks for both fixtures that literally say:
"No eccodes golden generated (eccodes unavailable at capture time); golden pending generation on internal cluster."

- gfswave_arctic_wind_drt40.grib2 (427269 bytes): GFS Wave arctic 9km polar-stereographic analysis, grid template 20 (polar stereographic), product template 0, data representation template 40 (JPEG2000), with a bitmap -- 1012036 grid points, 360052 present (ocean) points. Sourced from the noaa-gfs-bdp-pds S3 bucket.
- mrms_carib_refl_drt41.grib2 (28273 bytes): MRMS Caribbean reflectivity, grid template 0 (lat/lon), product template 0, data representation template 41 (PNG), 4500000 points, no bitmap. Sourced from the noaa-mrms-pds S3 bucket.

Confirmed by running the differential suite directly: with the jpeg2000 feature enabled, 'cargo test -p gribtract --test differential -- --nocapture' reports "Fixtures : 9 total (7 comparable, 2 no-golden)" -- these are exactly the 2 fixtures silently excluded from every agreement calculation. Real, already-downloaded NOAA data sits in the repo completely unverified against a reference decoder, which violates plan.md design principle 1 ("the oracle is the product") and principle 4 ("every disagreement becomes a permanent fixture").

eccodes is available in this environment via nix (confirmed: 'nix eval nixpkgs#eccodes.pname' succeeds and returns "eccodes"). Install via 'nix shell nixpkgs#eccodes' for the CLI tools (grib_dump, codes_info), or, if python eccodes bindings are not readily available, adapt scripts/gen_golden.py to shell out to codes_info or grib_dump with JSON output instead of importing the eccodes python module.

What to do:
1. Get eccodes (CLI or python bindings) working in this environment.

3. Commit the two golden JSON files (gfswave_arctic_wind_drt40.json and mrms_carib_refl_drt41.json) into the tests/corpus/golden directory.
4. Update the two provenance blocks in tests/corpus/manifest.json to remove the "golden pending" note.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both golden JSON files exist under tests/corpus/golden.
- 'cargo test -p gribtract --test differential --features jpeg2000 -- --nocapture' reports fixtures_no_golden reduced from 2 to 0, and either both fixtures match (fixtures_total=9, comparable=9, matched=9) or any real disagreement found is documented, not silently passed.

comments.text:
# bf-cmt1: Final Candidate File — Provenance Documentation

Compiles the verified findings of the bf-22pu → bf-2r5b → bf-qa5j chain into a
single self-contained provenance record for [bf-5yoa](bf-5yoa.md)
("Find and validate NOAA Lambert-conformal DRT=3 source file").

The chain located, accessibility-verified, and authoritatively (eccodes) decoded
NOAA GRIB2 files using **Grid Definition Template 3.30 (Lambert Conformal Conic)**
and **Data Representation Template 3 (complex packing + 2nd-order spatial
differencing)**. A primary candidate plus alternates are documented below.

---

## ★ Primary candidate (recommended)

**NAM awip12, winter analysis, smallest file in the set.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Direct download URL** | `https://noaa-nam-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/nam.20250115/nam.t00z.awip1200.tm00.grib2` |
| **Index (.idx) URL** | `https://noaa-nam-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/nam.20250115/nam.t00z.awip1200.tm00.grib2.idx` |
| **Model** | NOAA NAM (North American Mesoscale) |
| **Run date / cycle** | 2025-01-15, 00z (00:00 UTC) |
| **Forecast hour** | F00 (analysis — initial time step) |
| **Product / grid** | awip12 (AWIP 12-km physics grid, NCEP Grid 218) |
| **File size** | 26,364,442 B (25.1 MiB) |
| **Last-Modified** | Wed, 15 Jan 2025 01:39:19 GMT |
| **Messages** | 196 |

---

## Verification status (as of 2026-07-22)

| Check | Result | Method |
|---|---|---|
| **GDT 3.30** (Lambert Conformal) | ✅ **196/196 messages** | `grib_get gridDefinitionTemplateNumber` → all `30` (eccodes) |
| **DRT 3** (complex packing, spatial differencing) | ✅ **196/196 messages** | `grib_get dataRepresentationTemplateNumber` → all `3`; `packingType=grid_complex_spatial_differencing` (eccodes) |
| **URL accessible** | ✅ HTTP 200, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `Content-Type: binary/octet-stream` | `curl -sI` (live, 2026-07-22) |
| **Size matches** | ✅ `Content-Length: 26364442` = documented 26,364,442 B | `curl -sI` |
| **Valid GRIB2** | ✅ magic `4752 4942 0000 0002` ("GRIB", discipline=0, edition=2) | `curl -s -r 0-7 <url> \| xxd` |
| **Index present** | ✅ `.idx` returns HTTP 200 | `curl -sI <url>.idx` |

All four NAM files in the set were decoded the same way — **1046/1046 messages
are GDT 3.30 + DRT=3** (see [bf-qa5j](bf-qa5j.md)).

> **Caveat on the project's own decoder:** `gribtract-cli list` cannot yet read
> these files — DRT=3 unpacking is not implemented (fails with
> `error: buffer too short: need 0, got 262792`). eccodes is the ground-truth
> verifier used here, the same tool the project uses for golden generation.

---

## Grid parameters — NCEP Grid 218 (Lambert Conformal), message 1

Extracted authoritatively via `grib_get` / `grib_dump -j` (eccodes). The `awip12`
and `awphys` NAM files share the identical grid (verified: same GDT/Nx/Ny/La1/Lo1).

| Parameter (GRIB2 key) | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `gridDefinitionTemplateNumber` | **30** | Lambert Conformal Conic |
| `gridType` | `lambert` | — |
| `shapeOfTheEarth` | 6 | spherical, R = 6,371,229 m |
| `Nx` (Ni) | 614 | points along a parallel |
| `Ny` (Nj) | 428 | points along a meridian |
| `numberOfDataPoints` | 262,792 | = 614 × 428 |
| `latitudeOfFirstGridPointInDegrees` (**La1**) | 12.19 °N | first grid point lat |
| `longitudeOfFirstGridPointInDegrees` (**Lo1**) | 226.541 °E (= 133.459 °W) | first grid point lon |
| `LaDInDegrees` (**LaD**) | 25 °N | latitude where Dy is specified |
| `LoVInDegrees` (**LoV**) | 265 °E (= 95 °W) | grid orientation longitude |
| **Latin1** / **Latin2** | 25 °N / 25 °N | standard parallels |
| **Dx** / **Dy** | 12,191 m / 12,191 m | **12.191 km** resolution |
| scanning mode byte | `0x40` | +i, +j; `iScansNegatively`=0, `jPointsAreConsecutive`=0 |
| `centre` / `subCentre` | `kwbc` (7) / 0 | NCEP |

> **La2 / Lo2 (last grid point):** eccodes does not expose
> `latitudeOfLastGridPoint` / `longitudeOfLastGridPoint` for Lambert Conformal
> (3.30) — confirmed `<absent>` in `grib_dump -j`. Per the published NCEP Grid 218
> definition the last grid point is **La2 ≈ 47.442 °N, Lo2 ≈ 357.476 °E
> (2.524 °W)**; documented rather than file-derived.

## Packing detail — DRT 3 (template 5.3), message 1

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `dataRepresentationTemplateNumber` | **3** (template 5.3) |
| `packingType` | `grid_complex_spatial_differencing` |
| `bitsPerValue` | 15 |
| `orderOfSpatialDifferencing` | 2 (second-order) |
| `referenceValue` (R) | 9.94887 × 10⁶ |
| `binaryScaleFactor` (E) | 4 |
| `decimalScaleFactor` (D) | 2 |

`grid_complex_spatial_differencing` is eccodes' name for GRIB2 template 5.3,
confirming DRT=3 is complex packing **with** spatial differencing (vs. 5.2).

---

## Download method & access requirements

- **Access:** public HTTPS, **no authentication**. Served from AWS Open Data
  (`noaa-nam-pds` S3 bucket, `server: AmazonS3`,
  `x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256`).
- **Range support:** `Accept-Ranges: bytes` — partial/byte-range downloads work,
  and each `.idx` allows subsetting individual variables without the full file.
- **Reproducible fetch:**
  ```bash
  URL='https://noaa-nam-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/nam.20250115/nam.t00z.awip1200.tm00.grib2'
  curl -sI "$URL" | awk 'tolower($1)~/^(http|content-length|last-modified|accept-ranges)/{print}'
  curl -s -r 0-7 "$URL" | xxd        # expect: 4752 4942 0000 0002
  curl -sO "$URL"                    # full download (26 MB)
  ```
- **URL construction pattern:** `https://noaa-nam-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/nam.YYYYMMDD/nam.tHHz.awip12FF.tm00.grib2`
  where `HH` ∈ {00,06,12,18} and `FF` is the forecast hour.

---

## Alternates (all GDT 3.30 + DRT=3, accessibility-verified 2026-07-22)

For season/cycle/forecast-hour spread, or a fuller message set. All confirmed
GDT 3.30 + DRT=3 by eccodes in [bf-qa5j](bf-qa5j.md).

| File | URL (under `https://noaa-nam-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/`) | Size (B) | Run / F-hour | Msgs |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `nam.t12z.awip1200.tm00.grib2` | `nam.20240601/nam.t12z.awip1200.tm00.grib2` | 28,800,129 | 2024-06-01 12z, F00 (summer) | 196 |
| `nam.t12z.awip1206.tm00.grib2` | `nam.20240601/nam.t12z.awip1206.tm00.grib2` | 32,565,263 | 2024-06-01 12z, F06 (forecast) | 208 |
| `nam.t00z.awphys00.tm00.grib2` | `nam.20250115/nam.t00z.awphys00.tm00.grib2` | 52,938,055 | 2025-01-15 00z, F00 (awphys, fuller) | 446 |
| HRRR `wrfsfcf00/f03` | `noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/hrrr.YYYYMMDD/conus/hrrr.tHHz.wrfsfcfFF.grib2` | 130–143 MB | CONUS 3 km | — |

> **bf-we8d data-quality note:** that earlier bead listed the 2024-06-01 F00
> awip12 file as 30,259,561 B; the server's actual `Content-Length` is
> **28,800,129 B** (confirmed twice on 2026-07-22). Figures here come from live
> HEAD requests. HRRR files were not eccodes-decoded in bf-qa5j — the four NAM
> files already gave four independent confirmations at ¼–⅕ the byte cost.

---

## Provenance chain (full audit trail)

| Bead | Contribution |
|---|---|
| [bf-63ow](bf-63ow.md) | Researched NOAA regional model archives for Lambert-conformal candidates |
| [bf-37db](bf-37db.md) | Located Lambert-conformal DRT=3 candidate files |
| [bf-we8d](bf-we8d.md) | Extracted NAM awip12 URLs + metadata (size since corrected) |
| [bf-22pu](bf-22pu.md) | Verified URL accessibility + file sizes (HTTP 200, magic, `.idx`) |
| [bf-2r5b](bf-2r5b.md) | Live-verified all candidate URLs + sizes against `Content-Length` (2026-07-22) |
| [bf-qa5j](bf-qa5j.md) | **Authoritatively decoded** all 1046 msgs via eccodes — confirmed GDT 3.30 + DRT=3, documented grid + packing |
| **bf-cmt1** (this) | Compiles the above into final provenance + comments [bf-5yoa](bf-5yoa.md) |

Research doc: [docs/research/bf-2r5b-gdt330-drt3-candidate-files.md](../docs/research/bf-2r5b-gdt330-drt3-candidate-files.md)

comments.text:
# Candidate NOAA Ensemble Products with PDT 4.1 or 4.8

## Research Summary

Based on the parent bead (bf-3wkqt) research on NOAA ensemble products, here are the top candidate products that definitively use PDT 4.1 or 4.8:

---

## Candidate 1: GEFS Individual Members (PDT 4.1)

**Product Name:** GEFS (Global Ensemble Forecast System) - Individual Ensemble Members  
**Model Name:** GEFS  
**PDT Type:** 4.1 - Individual ensemble forecast, control and perturbed  
**Forecast Cycle:** 00z, 06z, 12z, 18z (4 cycles per day)  
**File Naming Pattern:**
- Control: `gec00.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fXXX`
- Perturbed: `gepNN.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fXXX` (NN = 01-30)

**Public Archive Access:** ✅ Confirmed
- Official NCEP archive: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/gens/
- NOMADS access: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/
- Direct FTP: ftp://ftp.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gens/prod/

**Typical File Size:** ~20-50 MB per forecast file (estimated based on 0.5° resolution global ensemble data)

**Why This Product:**
- Definitive PDT 4.1 usage (individual ensemble members)
- High public accessibility (multiple access methods)
- Regular production schedule (4x daily)
- Well-documented format

---

## Candidate 2: SREF Probability/Uncertainty Products (PDT 4.8)

**Product Name:** SREF (Short Range Ensemble Forecast) - Probability and Uncertainty Products  
**Model Name:** SREF  
**PDT Type:** 4.8 - Statistical processing (probability forecasts, uncertainty products)  
**Forecast Cycle:** 03z, 09z, 15z, 21z (4 cycles per day)  
**File Naming Pattern:**
- Mean: `sref.tCCz.pgrbXXX.mean.FHHH.grib2`
- Spread: `sref.tCCz.pgrbXXX.spread.FHHH.grib2`
- Probability: `sref.tCCz.pgrbXXX.prob.FHHH.grib2`
- Uncertainty: `sref.tCCz.pgrbXXX.UC.FHHH.grib2` (Max, Min, Mode, percentiles)

**Public Archive Access:** ✅ Confirmed
- Official NCEP archive: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/sref/
- NOMADS access: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/
- Direct FTP: ftp://ftp.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/sref/prod/

**Typical File Size:** ~5-30 MB per file (smaller than GEFS due to regional domain and fewer members)

**Why This Product:**
- Definitive PDT 4.8 usage (statistical processing: averages, probabilities, extremes)
- Regional scale (more manageable file sizes)
- Multiple statistical product types (mean, spread, prob, UC)
- Public access confirmed

---

## Candidate 3: NAEFS Anomaly/EFI Products (PDT 4.8)

**Product Name:** NAEFS (North American Ensemble Forecast System) - Anomaly and Extreme Forecast Index Products  
**Model Name:** NAEFS (52 members: 31 GEFS + 21 GEPS)  
**PDT Type:** 4.8 - Statistical processing (anomaly, extreme forecast index)  
**Forecast Cycle:** 00z, 06z, 12z, 18z (4 cycles per day)  
**File Naming Pattern:**
- Anomaly: `naefs_geavg.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50_anvfHHH`
- Climate Percentile: `naefs_geavg.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50_anfHHH`
- Extreme Forecast Index: `naefs_geefi.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50_bcfHHH`

**Public Archive Access:** ✅ Confirmed
- Official NCEP archive: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/naefs/
- NAEFS Situational Awareness: https://satable.ncep.noaa.gov/naefs/
- NOMADS access: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/

**Typical File Size:** ~10-40 MB per file (medium complexity, 52-member ensemble products)

**Why This Product:**
- Definitive PDT 4.8 usage (anomaly calculations, extreme forecast index)
- Multi-model ensemble (NOAA + Environment Canada)
- Multiple statistical product variants
- Public access confirmed

---

## Summary Table

| Product | PDT | Members | Cycle | Resolution | Archive Access | File Size Est. |
|---------|-----|---------|-------|------------|----------------|----------------|
| GEFS Individual | 4.1 | 31 | 00,06,12,18z | 0.5° global | ✅ Public | ~20-50 MB |
| SREF Prob/UC | 4.8 | 7 | 03,09,15,21z | ~16-40km regional | ✅ Public | ~5-30 MB |
| NAEFS Anomaly/EFI | 4.8 | 52 | 00,06,12,18z | 0.5° NA | ✅ Public | ~10-40 MB |

---

## Recommendation Priority

1. **Primary Target: GEFS Individual Members (PDT 4.1)** - Most straightforward individual ensemble data, excellent public access
2. **Secondary Target: SREF Probability Products (PDT 4.8)** - Multiple statistical processing types, smaller file sizes
3. **Tertiary Target: NAEFS Anomaly Products (PDT 4.8)** - Complex multi-model ensemble, advanced statistical processing

All three products have confirmed public archive access and well-documented GRIB2 structures.

---

- Parent bead bf-3wkqt research notes: ./notes/bf-3wkqt.md
- NCEP GRIB2 Documentation: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/docs/grib2/grib2_doc/

- NAEFS Products: https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/naefs/
- NOMADS: https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/

title: Add integration test coverage for gribtract-cli (decode, list, dump subcommands have zero tests)
description:
crates/gribtract-cli/src/main.rs is 268 lines implementing 3 real subcommands: decode (prints JSON), list (prints a metadata inventory), and dump (prints hex), each calling the real gribtract decode function -- this is NOT the "4-line stub" that bead bf-4nam (open, dated 2026-07-02) describes; that older bead's premise is stale (worth noting, but not the subject of this bead -- do not touch bf-4nam). Despite being a documented, real deliverable (README CLI section, plan.md Phase 7 "Publish + integrate" marked complete), there is zero test coverage:
- Searching crates/gribtract-cli for any file with "test" in the name returns nothing.
- Searching crates/gribtract-cli/src/main.rs for a test attribute returns nothing.
- No crates/gribtract-cli/tests directory exists at all.

This means none of the 3 subcommands -- the actual thing an end user or downstream integration runs -- are exercised by cargo test. A regression in JSON field-printing, list-inventory formatting, or error handling on a bad or missing input file would not be caught by the existing test suite.

Scope (keep this narrow -- use existing corpus fixtures, no new fixture sourcing needed):
1. Add an integration test file under crates/gribtract-cli/tests (e.g. cli.rs) using assert_cmd, or plain std::process::Command, to invoke the built binary.
2. Test the decode subcommand against the small gfs_anl_t2m_5x5 fixture in tests/corpus/small: exit code 0, stdout parses as valid JSON, contains the expected field count and parameter.
3. Test the list subcommand against the same fixture: exit code 0, stdout contains the field_count key.
4. Test the dump subcommand against the same fixture: exit code 0, produces hex output.
5. Test all 3 subcommands against a nonexistent file path: nonzero exit code, an error message on stderr, no panic.

Acceptance criteria:
- crates/gribtract-cli/tests/cli.rs (or equivalent) exists with at least the 5 cases above.
- cargo test -p gribtract-cli passes.
- While writing the test, manually verify it actually exercises the CLI output by temporarily breaking one subcommand (e.g. commenting out the JSON field loop) and confirming the new test fails; then restore the working code before committing.

title: Station benchmark bilinear agreement is not a correctness gate (42.9% published to dashboard)
description:
The plan (Phase 2c) and docs/notes/station-extraction-benchmark.md require nearest AND bilinear modes "each verified against full-grid decode at the points". The current verify() in xtask/src/bench_station.rs (around line 591) instead compares the bilinear-interpolated value against the NEAREST grid-point value with a 4x-packing-step tolerance — the comment admits it verifies the value is "physically reasonable, not to check equality". Result: bilinear agreement is published as 42.9% (see docs/notes/parse-speed-log.md Attempt 3 and bench-results.json), which is meaningless as a gate and alarming on the dashboard, where agreement is supposed to be the proof that speed numbers are correct.

What to do: verify the fast bilinear path against an independently computed reference bilinear at the same points — e.g. a naive straight-line reimplementation that takes the four corner values from the fully decoded grid (GridDefinition::bilinear_corners) and combines them with the same fractional weights, compared within derived tolerance. Bilinear-vs-bilinear should agree at ~100%; if it does not, that is a real bug in GridValues::bilinear (crates/gribtract-core/src/types.rs ~line 581) and must be fixed, not tolerated.

Acceptance criteria:
- verify() checks bilinear against a reference bilinear (equality within derived tolerance), not against the nearest value.
- Published bilinear agreement is a true gate (expected 100%); any deficit is investigated and fixed.
- The unchecked "Nearest and bilinear modes... verified" box in docs/notes/station-extraction-benchmark.md can be honestly ticked.
- bench-results.json regenerated so the dashboard no longer shows the 42.9% figure.

- Public access via HTTPS (no authentication required)

https://noaagefs.blob.core.windows.net/gefs/gefs.20210827/06/chem/pgrb2ap5/gefs.chem.t06z.a3d_0p50.f006.grib2
- Product: Chemistry model 3D output
- PDT: 4.1 (individual ensemble member)
- Resolution: 0.5° (a3d_0p50)
- Access: Public HTTPS, no authentication

### URL Pattern Templates

**Azure Blob Storage Pattern:**
https://noaagefs.blob.core.windows.net/gefs/gefs.YYYYMMDD/CC/{type}/{product}/{filename}
- Type: atmos, wave, chem
- Product: pgrb2ap5, pgrb2bp5, gridded
- Filename patterns:
  - Control: *.c00.*
  - Mean: geavg.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF
  - Spread: gespr.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF
  - Perturbed: gepNN.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF

**AWS S3 Pattern:**
https://noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gefs.YYYYMMDD/CC/atmos/pgrb2a/{filename}
- Control: gec00.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF
- Perturbed: gepNN.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF (NN = 01-30)
- Mean: geavg.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF
- Spread: gespr.tCCz.pgrb2a.0p50.fFFF

Where: YYYYMMDD = forecast date, CC = cycle hour (00/06/12/18), FFF = forecast hour (000-384)

### Data Centers and Access

**Azure Blob Storage (noaagefs.blob.core.windows.net)**
- Host: Microsoft Azure (via AI for Earth partnership)
- Access: Public HTTPS, no authentication required
- Rate limits: Standard Azure blob storage limits apply
- Retention: Recent operational data

**AWS S3 (noaa-gefs-pds.s3.amazonaws.com)**
- Host: AWS Open Data Registry
- Access: Public HTTPS, no authentication required
- Rate limits: Standard AWS rate limits apply
- Retention: Multi-decadal data (2017 to present)

- Total Members: 31 (1 control + 30 perturbed)
- Forecast Cycles: 4x daily (00Z, 06Z, 12Z, 18Z)
- Forecast Hours: FH000-FH384 (16 days, standard), extended to FH840 (00Z only, 35 days)
- PDT 4.1: Individual ensemble forecasts (control + perturbed members)
- PDT 4.8: Statistically processed products (mean, spread, bias-corrected)

description:
Problem: DRT=3 (complex packing with spatial differencing) cannot support true random access to individual grid points because each value depends on all prior values in the spatial differencing reversal step. The lazy DRT=3 path (see sibling bead for decode_point_drt3) must decode the full grid to extract any single point. When extracting values for N stations from the same field, this means N full grid decodes if called naively.

What to do: implement a decode-once-extract-many pattern for DRT=3 station extraction: decode the full grid once per field, store the result in a cache keyed by field identity (section 7 pointer or message hash), then do O(1) index lookups for each station. The cache lives for the duration of one forecast-hour extraction pass and is evicted between fields.

This is distinct from the geometry cache (already implemented) which caches grid-index-per-station. This is a value cache -- the decoded float grid -- which is the bottleneck for DRT=3.

Acceptance criteria:
- bench shows improved station_hours_per_sec for DRT=3 vs the naive N-decode path.
- Agreement remains 1.0 vs full-grid decode.
- The cache must NOT persist across distinct fields (different forecast hours have different packed values).

Notes: depends on the DRT=3 lazy path bead being done first. The optimization may be minor if fields.len() == 1 (single fixture bench); it matters when cycling through many forecast hours of the same grid.
